claims.text: Rapid solidification or thermomechanical processing can establish nonequilibrium chemical short-range order in metallic alloys.
The initial Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy is a metastable solid solution with identifiable short-range-order features.
Nonequilibrium short-range order biases elemental partitioning when the alloy is subsequently thermally activated.
Mg preferentially partitions during elevated-temperature exposure.
Other reactive elements preferentially partition during elevated-temperature exposure.
Thermal exposure of a solid-solution-containing alloy can lead to formation of an intermetallic phase.
Mg and reactive-element segregation promotes the nucleation and growth of intermetallic compounds.
The resulting intermetallic compounds form both along grain boundaries and within the matrix.
The intermetallic compounds capture or sequester key oxide-forming elements from the continuous matrix.
Sequestration of oxide-forming elements disrupts the formation of a continuous, uniformly protective oxide scale.
Disruption of the protective oxide scale causes a loss of corrosion resistance.
Disruption of the protective oxide scale causes a loss of high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The as-processed baseline has a uniform distribution of oxide-forming elements.
The as-processed baseline exhibits robust corrosion and oxidation resistance.
Elevated-temperature aging will increase the volume fraction of intermetallic phases relative to the initial state.
Intermetallic-phase growth will coincide with reduced continuity and protectiveness of surface oxide films.
Temperatures above approximately 600 degrees Celsius constitute a critical regime in which diffusion and phase transformations become significant.
Above approximately 600 degrees Celsius, diffusion-driven partitioning and intermetallic growth are accelerated.
Below approximately 600 degrees Celsius, transformation kinetics are minimal.
Below approximately 600 degrees Celsius, the original corrosion and oxidation resistance is maintained.
